Display options shared by all plot functions

Source: R/core-theme.R
wgh_plot_options.Rd

Every plot function and plot() method in the package accepts these options through ..., so any figure can be tuned without rewriting it. wgh_plot_options() documents them and can also be called to build an options list, for example to reuse the same settings for several plots with do.call().

Usage

wgh_plot_options(
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  x_label = NULL,
  y_label = NULL,
  colour_label = NULL,
  base_size = 11,
  legend = "bottom",
  palette = NULL,
  point_size = NULL,
  line_width = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  show_ci = TRUE,
  facet = NULL,
  facet_scales = "fixed",
  ncol = NULL,
  x_limits = NULL,
  y_limits = NULL,
  theme = NULL
)

Arguments

title, subtitle, caption

Plot title, subtitle and caption.

x_label, y_label, colour_label

Axis and legend titles.

base_size

Base font size of the theme.

legend

Legend position: "bottom", "right", "top", "left" or "none".

palette

Colours for the colour and fill scales: an unnamed vector (used in order) or a vector named by group (for example c(Male = "black", Female = "grey50")).

point_size, line_width, alpha

Size of points, width of lines and transparency, where the plot uses them.

show_ci

Show confidence or prediction bands, where available.

facet

A column to facet by, overriding the plot's default, or FALSE for no facets where the plot facets by default.

facet_scales

"fixed", "free", "free_x" or "free_y".

ncol

Number of facet columns.

x_limits, y_limits

Axis limits (zoom without dropping data).

theme

A complete ggplot2 theme replacing theme_wgh().

Value

A list of class wgh_plot_options.

Examples

cl <- wgh_classify(growdat)
pv <- wgh_prevalence(cl[cl$age >= 5, ], "obesity", by = c("sex", "yearvisit"))
# The same plot with different display options
wgh_plot_prevalence(pv)

wgh_plot_prevalence(pv, title = "Obesity, 5 to 18 years", base_size = 14,
                    palette = c(Male = "black", Female = "grey60"), show_ci = FALSE,
                    y_limits = c(0, 40), legend = "right")
#> Warning: No shared levels found between `names(values)` of the manual scale and the
#> data's fill values.

# Reuse a set of options
opts <- wgh_plot_options(base_size = 9, legend = "none")
do.call(wgh_plot_prevalence, c(list(pv), opts))
